label: The resume branch of the Gate 3 classifier applies a read-only override that the module's own decision order (gate-3-classifier.ts:786, 'resume or memory_save ... ALWAYS required') forbids: memory-save returns triggersGate3 true unconditionally at :837 while the resume branch returns false when a read-only disqualifier matched at :843, so 'review the packet then resume it' suppresses Gate 3 where 'review the packet then save it' asks. Change gate-3-classifier.ts:841-845 to return { triggersGate3: true, reason: 'resume_match' } exactly as the memory-save branch does; expected after fix is that every resume phrase triggers Gate 3 and read_only_override becomes reachable only from the file-write branch. Verify: node -e classifyPrompt('review the validation rules then resume the packet').reason. Release attribution v4.0.0.1 inherited from the run registry, not re-derived this iteration; confidence 0.9.

The ANCHORS_VALID phase-parent exemption in orchestrator.ts:975-977 is a blanket pass that returns before any anchor is parsed, not a narrowed requirement: a phase parent's spec.md is template-backed (orchestrator.ts:636 maps phase+spec.md to phase-parent.spec.md.tmpl) yet an unclosed anchor there passes the rule that exists to catch it while the same defect one folder down fails. Change orchestrator.ts:975-977 to skip only the 'no anchors found' finding and the required-template-section list for a phase parent, and still run duplicate/unbalanced/nesting detection over authored anchors; expected after fix is that a phase parent with an unmatched opener reports an integrity issue while a lean anchor-free phase parent still passes. Verify: copy a phase parent to /tmp, delete one closing ANCHOR line, run validate.sh <packet> --strict (today reports pass). Confidence 0.85.

check-goal.cjs has two exit ladders: packet mode distinguishes errors (return 2) from not-passed (return 1) at :718, but corpus mode keys on report.errors.length alone at :703, so a warnings-only packet makes 'check-goal.cjs --all' exit 0 while the same packet by name exits 1. CI sweeps are the caller most likely to use the corpus form, which makes them the caller most damaged. Change check-goal.cjs:700-704 to mirror the packet ladder (errors>0 -> 2, else passed ? 0 : 1) and surface a passed flag from scanWorkspace alongside errors/warnings; expected after fix is that the corpus and packet forms agree on every packet. Verify: node .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/check-goal.cjs --all; echo $? against the same packet by name. Confidence 0.85.

check-goal.cjs resolves a relative packet argument against the workspace root taken at :698 rather than the caller's directory at :706, and only --root changes that root (:568), so an operator who cds into a packet and passes '.' silently checks the repository root - the corpus path of f-iter013-003 - with no warning that the argument was reinterpreted. Change check-goal.cjs:706 to resolve options.packetArg against process.cwd() when that resolution exists and fall back to workspaceRoot only otherwise; expected after fix is that 'cd specs/<track>/<packet> && check-goal.cjs .' reports packet=<that packet> while 'check-goal.cjs specs/...' from the root is unchanged. Verify: cd /tmp/<copy>/specs/<packet> && node /tmp/<copy>/.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-goal/scripts/check-goal.cjs . Confidence 0.9.

resolveProjectRoot at config.ts:131-147 writes a stderr warning and returns the runtime repository as the project root when neither the git top level nor cwd uses spec-kit (:142, :146), and that value is bound into STATIC_CONFIG.PROJECT_ROOT at module load (:355), so every consequence - memory files, index, workspace scans - lands inside the shipped skill tree of a repo the caller never named. A stderr line during a long run is not a gate. Change config.ts:131-147 to throw or return a discriminated miss when no explicit override was supplied, letting the CLI name the --root/env escape hatch; expected after fix is that running a spec-kit CLI outside a spec-kit repository fails loudly instead of writing into the runtime repository, with the runtime repo reachable only by explicit opt-in. Verify: cd /tmp && run a spec-kit CLI with --help (read-only) and inspect which root it resolves. Fallback is deliberate per the message text, which is why this is type 4 not type 3; confidence 0.8.

create.sh assigns TEMPLATES_BASE="${SPECKIT_TEMPLATES_BASE:-$REPO_ROOT/...}" three times at three depths (create.sh:1477 inside resolve_and_validate_create_target, :1665 in the PHASE_MODE block, :2253 in the main flow) with the only existence check on the last site (:2259), so every consumer in between - including the phase child scaffolder that reads the global at :1219 - trusts the value unchecked and an SPECKIT_TEMPLATES_BASE typo surfaces as 'copy_template failed for <doc>' from mid-scaffold rather than as a root error. Change create.sh:1409 to hold one readonly assignment plus the -d check immediately after REPO_ROOT is resolved and delete the three later assignments; expected after fix is one value, one validation, and a bad root failing before the first mkdir. Verify: SPECKIT_TEMPLATES_BASE=/nope bash -x create.sh ... and confirm today's failure comes from copy_template. Confidence 0.85.

The 'skip' severity tier has no producer: RegistrySeverity includes 'skip' at orchestrator.ts:107 and shouldRunRegistryShellRule guards it first at :452, but the shipped registry holds 42 rules split 32 error / 8 warn / 2 info and none at 'skip', so the guard marks where a future reader will look for the rule-disabling switch and finds nothing. Nothing breaks if removed - the registry would need a 'skip' row first, and adding one is a one-line type change; removing the tier also removes its ambiguity with strict_only, which is consumed one line later at :453. Change orchestrator.ts:107 and :452 to drop the tier, or add the producer. Confidence 0.9.

The level expression at orchestrator.ts:1383 (opts.strict && isPhaseParent(folder) ? 'phase' : detectLevel(folder)) is a no-op because detectLevel already returns 'phase' whenever the folder is a phase parent (orchestrator.ts:192), so both arms produce the same value for every input and the strict conjunct reads as if strictness altered level detection. Nothing breaks if replaced with detectLevel(folder) - the change is behaviour-identical; if the intent was ever 'strict judges a phase parent as a phase', state it as an assertion with the test that proves it rather than a ternary that cannot fail. Confidence 0.9.

The five canonical-save .sh/.cjs pairs are shims, not duplicate implementations, which closes the Q9 residual: each .sh is 53 lines whose only real line delegates with output="$(node "$CANONICAL_SAVE_MODULE" "$folder")" (check-canonical-save-root-spec.sh:34 and four siblings), so the shape is bash wrapper -> one node implementation. Nothing breaks if the wrappers stay, and removing them would mean teaching the orchestrator to dispatch rules/check-*.cjs - a change with no behavioural payoff. Recommendation: leave as-is and record the shape so a later pass does not re-open it as suspected duplication; cost is one extra process per rule, five rules per run. Confidence 0.95.

Two root-resolution strategies coexist in one product: sk-create-goal resolves its workspace root from __dirname (check-goal.cjs:59) while spec-kit core walks to the git top level and tests for a spec-kit marker (config.ts:135). A module-relative default is right for a script shipped inside the skill and wrong the moment the skill is vendored or invoked through a linked path - precisely the case resolveProjectRoot exists to handle - and two answers to 'where is the workspace' is the sk-code canon's named drift. Change check-goal.cjs:58-60 to call the spec-kit resolver with the module-relative path as a last resort; expected after fix is that --root, cwd discovery and the vendored default resolve through one function and the report's packet= label stops depending on where the script sits. Confidence 0.8.

validator-registry.json holds 42 rules: 33 rules/check-*.sh, 5 ts:spec-doc-structure, 3 validation/*.ts, 1 native:orchestrator. Severity split 32 error / 8 warn / 2 info, zero skip. Every .sh in runtime/cli/rules is registered; the 5 *.cjs and 4 *-helper modules are support files, not rules.

create.sh is 2443 lines against validate.sh's 523; the bulk concentrates in the PHASE_MODE block (create.sh:1660-2170) and the template-root duplication is a 3-site, 1-check pattern (1477, 1665, 2253 with the check at 2259).

A rule-availability flag that no shipped configuration can produce is indistinguishable from a rule that cannot be disabled; the registry is the only producer for severity and strict_only, so a tier with zero rows is dead surface.

When one command exposes two entry forms (single target vs corpus sweep) over the same checks, the two forms must agree on the verdict for every shared target or the sweep cannot be trusted as a gate.

direction: Treating the canonical-save .sh/.cjs pairs as duplicate implementations and proposing consolidation
reason: All five .sh files are 53-line delegating shims whose only executable line calls the paired .cjs; there is one implementation per rule, so consolidation would buy nothing and would break the registry's rules/check-*.sh dispatch contract.

direction: Reading create.sh's three TEMPLATES_BASE assignments as an unset-variable bug on the phase path
reason: In PHASE_MODE the assignment at create.sh:1665 executes before the phase block reaches the child scaffolder that reads the global at :1219, so the value is always set there; the defect is late validation and triplication, not an empty value.
